You are researching the local marketing ecosystem for a new dining-district brand in Danville, California ("Danville Dining District" / "South of Hartz" / #danvilleafterdark). The district is four restaurants at the south end of Hartz Avenue downtown: Rancho Cantina, Incontro Ristorante, Kaia's Island Kitchen & Tiki Bar, and Harvest. The partners want late-night (8-10pm) traffic, industry nights, cross-visits (dinner at one, nightcap/dessert at another), and later to invite the chamber of commerce, other Danville businesses and local influencers to join.
Tools: use WebSearch and WebFetch (load them with ToolSearch "select:WebSearch,WebFetch" first). You may also use Bash with curl (e.g. curl -sL -A "Mozilla/5.0" URL | head -c 200000) to read pages that WebFetch cannot, and curl -sI to check headers. Never guess: every fact must come from a page you actually read. If something cannot be found, leave it empty and say so in notes. Do not invent hours, prices, or dishes.
Find: (1) The Danville Area Chamber of Commerce (name, URL, contact, membership/marketing programs, any restaurant-week or "shop local" programs). (2) Other town organizations: Discover Danville / Town of Danville economic development, Downtown Danville business association, Danville Parks & Rec events. (3) Recurring downtown events that draw evening crowds (Hot Summer Nights car show, Danville Farmers' Market, Lighting of the Old Oak Tree, Fourth of July parade, art walks, Devil Mountain Run, Blackhawk events) with dates/URLs. (4) Local food media and influencers: Diablo Magazine, Danville SanRamon.com, Patch, East Bay food Instagram accounts and Danville/Tri-Valley foodie accounts (handles + follower counts if visible), local podcasts. (5) Hashtags currently used for Danville dining/nightlife (#danvilleca #downtowndanville #eastbayeats etc.). (6) Any existing "restaurant week", "dine around" or passport programs in Danville/San Ramon/Tri-Valley that the district could plug into. Cite sources. Return only the structured object.

## Event Details

The Town of Danville invites the community to celebrate Independence Day at the annual Kiwanis-Danville 4th of July Parade, hosted by the Kiwanis Club of the San Ramon Valley in partnership with the Town. The parade will take place Saturday, July 4, from 9 a.m. to noon along Hartz Avenue and San Ramon Valley Boulevard.

## Route and Location

The parade begins at San Ramon Valley High School near Railroad Avenue and continues along Hartz Avenue and San Ramon Valley Boulevard, ending at Town and Country Drive.

## Participation

The parade will feature more than 100 participating groups, and thousands of spectators are expected to line the route for one of Danville's most anticipated summer celebrations. 2026 marks the 51st anniversary that the Kiwanis Club of San Ramon Valley first began organizing and conducting the 4th of July Parade in Danville, and Kiwanis has presented a Parade every year since, including the virtual Parade that was held online in COVID year 2020.

## Parking and Access

Parking is expected to be limited, so parade-goers are encouraged to walk or bike. Parade-goers may consider parking at the Sycamore Park & Ride parking lot, and using the Iron Horse Trail to walk downtown.

## Danville Business Alliance (Pennsylvania)

The Danville Business Alliance focuses on the development and beautification of downtown Danville, Pennsylvania, while supporting local businesses and orchestrating community events. The organization serves as the community's convener of public and private sector resources, experts, and entrepreneurs intent on making downtown Danville a livable and vibrant district.

### Key Initiatives and Services

The Economic Vitality Committee (EVC) supports new developments, catalytic projects, and entrepreneurs seeking to open or relocate a business in Danville. The Design Committee spearheads major art projects such as public murals, a bike rack initiative, planter contest, and holiday window contest, and also reviews applications from Mill Street business owners seeking matching grant funds for their façade renovations.

The Danville Business Alliance (DBA) is a member-based organization originally incorporated in the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania as Tomorrow's Vision, Inc. in 2001, changed its name to the DBA in 2004, and in 2006 the Internal Revenue Service determined it was a tax exempt organization under section 501(c)(3).

content.content:
# Danville Day Trip Summary

## Downtown Danville & Streets

Danville's downtown centers on **Hartz Avenue**, described as having "an air of business" with charming shops. The area features historic buildings including the original **Grange Hall (built 1874)** and the **Danville Hotel (opened 1890s)**. Street names honor local pioneers like Harlan and Boone.

## Restaurants & Bars

**Morning:**
- **Maison Benoit** (402 Railroad Ave.) - French bakery, won Best Croissant San Francisco competition

**Evening Options:**
- **Kaia's Island Kitchen & Tiki Bar** (480 Hartz Ave.) - Hawaiian cuisine with tropical drinks
- **Albi's** - New Middle Eastern beer garden with grilled kebabs
- **Sushi Tamahime** - Japanese authentic nigiri and set meals
- **Taverna Sorrentina** (100 Railroad Ave.) - Italian restaurant opened last year by three Naples friends

## Town Facts

- **Population:** Approximately 43,000
- **Wealth ranking:** 17th-richest community in the U.S. (2023)
- **History:** Gold Rush era settlement named for an early settler's mother-in-law from Danville, Kentucky
- **Notable landmark:** Mount Diablo looms nearby; Eugene O'Neill National Historic Site (Tao House) celebrated its 50th anniversary in 2026

# Danville, California - Key Facts

**Population (2020 Census):** 43,582

**Median Household Income (2023):** $223,206

**Incorporation Year:** July 1, 1982

**County:** Contra Costa

**Downtown/Hartz Avenue History:**
John Hartz sold 8.65 acres for the railroad depot and subdivided land east of the station. "The Danville Hotel originally sat across from the station and was moved to face Hartz" Avenue in 1927, shifting the town center from Front Street.

**Iron Horse Trail:**
A converted railroad now serves as "a 10-foot-wide (3.0 m) path that consists of biking and hiking trails." It extends from Livermore to Concord, passing through Danville.

**Notable Landmarks:**
- Eugene O'Neill National Historic Site (Tao House)
- Village Theatre and Art Gallery
- Museum of the San Ramon Valley (housed in the restored 1891 Southern Pacific depot)
- Old Oak Tree (Annual Lighting ceremony held Friday after Thanksgiving on Diablo Road)

**Nickname/Slogan:** 
"Heart of the San Ramon Valley" and the town motto is "Live Locally"

## Discover Danville Walking Tour App

Discover Danville is an interactive walking tour app that provides a unique way to explore Danville, including historic landmarks, charming local shops and delightful restaurants. The web-based Discover Danville app is available on smartphones to tour historic sites, restaurants, and retail shops around Town.

## Features

The web-based app offers location-based pinpoint locations for Downtown Danville and beyond. The app also features historical context, allowing users to view photos of "what used to be" while walking through Downtown Danville.

## Purpose

## Project Overview

Hearts of Danville is a new temporary public art project that will bring creativity and vibrant seasonal energy to downtown in winter 2027. Running from January through March 2027, the project will feature sixteen tabletop-sized heart sculptures, each standing 17 inches tall and transformed by a local artist into a one-of-a-kind work of art.

## Location and Display

The completed sculptures will be displayed in community buildings and local businesses throughout Downtown Danville for all to enjoy.

## Community Participation

Artists are invited to submit design proposals for a heart sculpture. Each selected artist will use a tabletop-sized heart sculpture as a canvas for original artwork. Additionally, downtown businesses are invited to apply to host a completed heart sculpture at their location during the project. Sponsors are invited to support the creation of each heart sculpture and help make the public art project possible.

## Related Gallery Exhibition

Hearts of Danville will also coincide with The Heart of It, the Winter 2027 art exhibition at the Village Theatre Art Gallery. Together, the gallery exhibition and downtown public art series will create a community-wide celebration of art, creativity, and connection during the winter season.

Here are the search results for the Eddy House/500 Hartz in Danville:

## Key Information

The Eddy House is a Queen Anne Cottage that was built in approximately 1903. The building, which is located at 500 Hartz Ave., is now home to the popular Danville Harvest Restaurant.

## Historical Details

This one story clapboard structure has a pyramidal hipped roof and single front gable, with a partial width porch, turned porch supports and two pane windows.

Members of the Eddy family lived in the home continuously from 1903 to 1946. Although they were not particularly well known, they were descendants of Leonard Eddy who built a cabin in the Danville area in 1853 as one of the first U.S. settlers.

## Preservation

The house was nearly demolished in 1988, but the demolition permit was denied when the historic significance of the house was brought to the attention of Town officials.

## Notable Features

A separate structure, since removed, at the rear of the property served as the first San Ramon Valley Union High School in 1910. As a side note, one of the Eddy's was married to a relative of Walt Disney, who had visited the home.

This parking lot is located adjacent to the Library/Community Center located at 400
Front Street. It contains 86 parking spaces with and is designated as 4-hour parking, 7
a.m. and 6 p.m., Monday through Saturday, excluding Sundays and holidays. Use of
this parking facility is primarily designated and encouraged for patrons and visitors of
the Library and Community Center.

Rose Street Municipal Lot
The Rose Street Municipal Lot is located at the north end of Rose Avenue, north of
Linda Mesa Avenue. It contains approximately 17 parking spaces and is designated as
3-hour parking, 7 a.m. and 6 p.m., Monday through Saturday, excluding Sundays and
holidays. "All Day By Permit" parking is allowed within the entire lot.

Valet Parking Operations

Any business that wishes to operate private valet services within the Town must obtain
a Town of Danville encroachment permit. A detailed plan outlining the complete valet
service operation must also be submitted along with the encroachment permit
application. The Town will evaluate valet operation requests based on several criteria
including, but not limited to, potential use of public right-of-way, feasibility, and public
safety.

The Town of Danville Police Department is responsible for enforcing all parking
regulations throughout the Downtown. Focused parking enforcement efforts are
necessary to insure compliance with permit parking regulations, thereby insuring the
maximum available parking resources for business patrons.
